incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The First Board of Directors of the Company, acting provisionally, hereby resolves the following: (i) Subscription to the full share capital of the Company in accordance with the proportion and manner detailed in the draft bylaws; (ii) Adoption of the registered office at the address to be specified in the bylaws; (iii) Appointment of [Name] as Managing Director and [Name] as Corporate Secretary; (iv) Approval of the Company's Bylaws in the form presented; and (v) Authorization to file the incorporation documents with the Registro Mercantil, obtain the NIF, and commence the operational activities as an NVOCC. This resolution is adopted unanimously pursuant to the requirements of the Ley 1/2010 de Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada and ensures proper statutory incorporation and corporate governance setup.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – official portal www.agenciatributaria.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities forming a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must first obtain a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) from AEAT before the public deed is executed, then the final NIF is issued after registration in the Mercantile Registry. Non-resident foreign entities not established in Spain must apply for a NIF via AEAT Form 036/037 and obtain a Spanish VAT registration number. Private individuals acting as non-resident entrepreneurs obtain a NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero). The SL itself is then registered for Spanish Corporate Income Tax (IS) and VAT (IVA) using the same NIF.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Spanish SL is tax-resident in Spain if it is incorporated under Spanish law, has its registered seat in Spain, or has its effective place of management in Spain. It is subject to Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) on its worldwide income unless the territoriality exception for permanent establishments abroad applies. The SL is a separate legal person and no pass-through treatment is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain follows a classical entity-level taxation system with no check-the-box regime analogous to the US. However, a foreign entity may be re-characterized as a Spanish permanent establishment under the Corporate Income Tax Law if its activity is carried on through a fixed place of business in Spain. Tax group consolidation under the special regime (Régimen Especial de Grupos de Sociedades) is available for Spanish-resident groups with common control. Hybrid mismatch elections are governed by Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive (ATAD) transpositions in the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law, subject to factual substance and general anti-avoidance rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA) – governed by Ley 37/1992
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold for established taxable persons; any entity carrying out taxable supplies in Spain must register for IVA before commencing operations. Non-resident suppliers making B2B supplies subject to reverse charge have no registration threshold. For distance sales of goods from other EU Member States, the EUR 10,000 annual threshold applies before a Spanish registration becomes mandatory; once exceeded, full Spanish registration is required.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is mandatory for B2B transactions under Ley Crea y Crece and will be phased in via national regulations (RD 1006/2023), with software interoperability requirements. Large enterprises with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6,001,206 must file Immediate Supply of Information (SII) electronically to AEAT within 4 days of invoice issuance. Fiscal clearance is not a real-time stamping system analogous to Italy; however, all VAT records and invoices must be electronically transmitted under SII for large taxpayers, and the Verifactu system requires certification of software and invoice integrity.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Spanish customs territory to third countries and certain intra-Community supplies are exempt with credit (0% IVA). For an NVOCC ocean freight forwarding service, the following services may qualify for exemption as related to international transport: the transport of goods to a destination outside the EU, ancillary services directly related to the export of goods, and intermediary services provided on behalf of the exporter or consignor where the underlying operation is exempt. The service provider must obtain and retain documentary evidence proving the transport chain from the Spanish port to a destination outside the EU. Direct proof of movement of goods is required; mere handling of freight is not sufficient unless the NVOCC is acting as a principal or is directly linked to the physical export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo) bearing the correct exit presentation
Bill of Lading or Master Bill of Lading evidencing the sea carriage from an EU port to a non-EU port
Commercial Invoice / Freight Invoice and applicable Incoterms
Proof of physical exit from EU customs territory (e.g., stamped DUA by customs, terminal exit report, continuous supervision records)
Packing List and any required export licenses / certificates
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT confirmation evidencing receipt of consideration from the non-EU counterparty
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT rigorously scrutinises export zero-rating claims. If the exporter cannot present the complete documentary bundle within the statutory verification period, AEAT issues an assessment requiring the VAT previously zero-rated, plus late-payment interest. Fraudulent or false export zero-rating claims are treated as tax evasion under Ley General Tributaria, with penalties of 50% to 150% of the undue VAT amount, and in severe cases may constitute a criminal offence under the Spanish Criminal Code (delito contra la Hacienda Pública) with prison liability when the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000. Retrospective clawback may extend to previous tax periods within a 4-year limitation period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the European System of Central Banks and in coordination with the Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias (SEPBLAC) and the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) for customs and balance-of-payments statistical control.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates a fully liberalized capital-movement regime under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. The euro is completely convertible, with no exchange controls on current-account transactions, dividends, interest, royalties, or capital inflows/outflows. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted after compliance with Spanish corporate formalities, including annual account approval, recognition of distributable reserves, dividend distribution agreements, and applicable withholding tax filings. No prior central bank approval is required, but statistical declaration to the Banco de España may be obligatory for cross-border transactions above EUR 10,000 or where the company is part of a foreign-owned group.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain does not impose export-proceeds surrender requirements or mandatory conversion ratios. Spanish resident NVOCCs may freely receive export and freight-forwarding proceeds in euro or foreign currency, maintain multicurrency accounts, and settle commercial obligations in the currency of the commercial contract. Nevertheless, all export/freight-service receipts must be matched to customs declarations and commercial invoices under AEAT requirements, total cross-border flows must be reported to the Banco de España for statistical purposes in accordance with Circular 4/2012, and cash payments exceeding EUR 10,000 are restricted under Law 10/2010 on anti-money-laundering prevention.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Trade & FX Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for transactional payment activity, Low for full treasury banking. EU-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) passported into Spain under PSD2 may lawfully provide cross-border payment accounts, multi-currency wallets, and payment-native FX conversion, but they are not credit institutions and therefore may not offer credit, escrow-grade deposits, overdrafts, or derivative-hedging products. Non-EU and offshore digital EMI platforms have limited or no regulatory viability in Spain and are generally declined by Spanish tax authorities and customs brokers for operational treasury purposes. The NVOCC should rely on a tier-1 Spanish bank for liquidity and use an EU-authorized EMI only as a supplementary collection rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal statutory mandate requiring corporate directors to appear physically before a bank for account opening. However, in practice, tier-1 commercial banks require remote-online identification through video verification or electronic signature using the Spanish electronic ID system, with the company's legal representative having a Spanish NIE/Tax Identification Number and valid passport/ID. For non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), most Spanish banks demand either an in-person branch interview at a commercial branch, a duly notarized and apostilled board resolution, or a certified power of attorney granting a resident representative authority to open and operate the account. Remote opening is generally feasible for an EU-incorporated parent with full KYC documentation, but the NVOCC's medium-risk classification and ISIC 5229 scope may trigger enhanced due diligence and an inevitable physical or video-recorded interview with the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering red flags: over/under-invoicing, duplicate bills of lading, discrepancies in declared cargo value, mixed cargo descriptions, or payments to third-party merchants not shown as the actual shipper or consignee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete commercial file for each shipment: signed booking confirmation, original master/house house bill of lading, Single Administrative Document / customs export-import declaration, commercial invoice and packing list, freight certificate, proof of container movement, ISF/safety-of-shipment filings, any customs clearance broker correspondence, and written contracts evidencing the NVOCC's legitimate role as contractual carrier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ultimate beneficial ownership or a shareholder/parent company located in a high-risk or sanctioned jurisdiction, or recent incorporation without operational history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized escritura pública (deed of incorporation), current certificate from the Registro Mercantil Central, Register of Beneficial Owners (Registro de Titularidades Reales), articles of association, a full corporate ownership chain with copies of identification of all UBOs, apostilled originals and official sworn Spanish translations, tax residency certificate of the parent, and an economic-nexus letter demonstrating the underlying freight-forwarding business rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening hits, politically exposed person (PEP) affiliations, or unexplained source-of-funds red flags arising from high-volume container traffic to embargoed or high-risk ports.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced KYC questionnaire, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations supported by audited financial statements, transaction-level accounting ledgers, charter-party or slot charter agreements, container ship dunnage reports, marine cargo insurance certificate, sanctions screening clearances from the bank's own compliance system, a business-risk self-assessment, and a written representation letter affirming no undeclared cargoes or dual-use goods are handled without a valid license.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from the non-resident parent or shareholders should be remitted in euro via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 (depending on whether the credit is posted directly to the Spanish SL's account or via a correspondent bank). The payment reference in field 70 (Remittance Information) must explicitly state the purpose, such as 'Capital contribution — aportación de capital' or 'Shareholder loan — préstamo entre empresas del grupo'. If the contribution is formalized as an equity increase, it must be approved by the shareholders' meeting, executed before a notary, and inscribed in the Mercantile Register; if structured as a shareholder loan, the loan agreement must be documented and reported in the corporate year-end financial statements. For Banco de España statistical purposes, the Spanish SL must file the balance-of-payments declaration when the cumulative cross-border transaction amount exceeds EUR 10,000. The company's Spanish NIF, EORI number, and bank account holding branch should be included in the wire instructions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound financial supply-chain disbursements for ocean freight and NVOCC trade settlement should be executed via SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier, port authority, or inland-carrier payments in non-euro currencies; high-value or high-risk transactions warrant the use of documentary letters of credit (commercial LCs) with the bank acting as confirming or advising institution. Within the eurozone and SEPA zone, SEPA Credit Transfers and SEPA Direct Debits are permissible for domestic and intra-EEA EUR settlements. All outbound payments must be backed by the corresponding shipping, customs, or service-provision invoice; payment authorization copies and FX settlement confirmations must be retained for AEAT, customs, and anti-money-laundering audit purposes. Crypto-backed rails, personal money transfer networks, and non-bank private clearing systems are impermissible for Irish-? [does not correspond to Spain] For Spanish treasury, crypto rails are not accepted as regulatory clearing rails; for this NVOCC, I will not include such a false mention. Instead: the use of commercial LCs and SWIFT MT103 is the compliant clearing standard, and the treasury must retain a statement of account showing the sequential payment chain from the Spanish SL to each counterparty.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD rolling forwards for ocean freight receivables and payables in USD
EUR/CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where underlying Chinese renminbi restrictions apply
EUR/CNY deliverable forwards via offshore liquidity channels
Cross-currency swaps between EUR and USD for principal and interest cash flows
Plain-vanilla EUR/USD and EUR/GBP currency swaps

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) – Modelo 200
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days following the six-month period after tax-year close; for calendar-year entities: 1 January – 25 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge scale of 5%/10%/15% plus late-payment interest; underpayment sanctions of 50%–100% of the assessed amount; prolonged non-filing may trigger administrative enforcement, embargo of assets, and criminal-tax referral where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office; centralized via Registro Mercantil Central
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual accounts must be approved within six months of year-end (by 30 June for calendar-year companies) and deposited within one month of approval (by 31 July for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-deposit penalty of EUR 200–2,000; continued non-deposit triggers 'cierre registral', barring registration of all subsequent corporate documents until accounts are filed; persistent non-deposit may lead to registry closure and administrative cancellation proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 and 28/29 February of the year following the relevant calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of EUR 100 per omitted or inaccurate counterparty record, plus a proportional sanction of up to 1% of affected transaction amounts; no direct strike-off, but repeated non-filing can be re-qualified as serious tax infringement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT summary return (Resumen Anual de IVA) – Modelo 390
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 – 30 January following the close of the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties under Article 198 of the General Tax Law, ranging from EUR 100 fixed penalties to 0.5%–2% of the declared balance; accumulating tax debt may lead to embargo and enforced collection, but does not directly trigger corporate strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is mandatory when the SL meets at least two of the following at year-end for two consecutive years: total assets exceed EUR 4,000,000; net annual turnover exceeds EUR 8,000,000; average workforce exceeds 50 employees. Companies forming a consolidation group and public-interest entities require audit irrespective of size. A company crossing these thresholds for the first time must appoint an auditor for that and the following year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad 2007, as amended); the PGC de PYMES may be used where the company meets the Article 257 LSC small-company thresholds; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is not mandatory for a standalone NVOCC SL unless it is a listed or consolidated group parent.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain imposes no standalone annual UBO return. Beneficial-ownership data must be kept current at all times; any share transfer or change in ultimate ownership must be formalized before a notary and filed with the Registro Mercantil through the 'Declaración de Titularidad Real' process. The annual Modelo 200 and annual accounts provide corroborative ownership disclosures. Failure to update UBO records after a share transfer is an AML infringement exposing the SL to fines of EUR 3,000–60,000.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors and Appointing Resolutions (as recorded and filed with Registro Mercantil)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,000 – USD 2,500 per year for a professional registered office and corporate secretarial agent in Spain
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 10,000 for a small-to-mid-size Spanish SL audit; nil when the statutory audit exemption applies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax due (25% applied to taxable base)

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 19% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% under most DTAs (0% with EU countries); Interest: 19% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% under most DTAs

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 20 million EUR for Local File; 50 million EUR for Master File

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties: fines up to 225% of evaded tax plus imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, disqualification from corporate management, possible imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining Spanish SL with no real business operations, employees or premises despite NVOCC licensing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax deductions, income recharacterization, fines up to 2 million euros
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil, personal tax liability, potential criminal charges

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file suspicious transaction reports or comply with cross-border transaction monitoring
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 2 million euros or 10% of annual turnover; criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, disqualification, imprisonment for aggravated cases
